COST LAW: the lane-2 record (CRYSTAL_STATUS 3c, eval_ir_bvar_range.rs, bundles.rs) reads its 0.021 / 0.431 / 6.586 s at W = 8 / 12 / 16 as a `2^W law`. Re-measured here at FIXED width with a varying dividend, the cost of ir_wrap w n is LINEAR IN n and INDEPENDENT of w: 1.322 / 2.644 / 5.399 s at w = 64 for n = 7000 / 14000 / 28000, and 1.356 s at w = 8 for n = 7000. The earlier points varied width and dividend together (its dividend was 2^W - 1 each time), so the x15.3 it saw is the x16 in the DIVIDEND. The ~5-day extrapolation it drew stands, at ~9.6 days by this law. Operationally the difference is total: `wide type => unaffordable` is false and would have refused is_valid_char, which is at width 64 and chains.
candidate_selection.why_this_body: Of the 177 fully-chainable codegen-flipped bodies, exactly TWO contain a condbr (expr::bvar_in_range, already chained, and this one) and they are the only two carrying a short-circuit as real control flow. This one is at width 64 -- twice the other's -- has BOTH a `||` and a `&&`, is the only chainable body that puts a materialised constant in an icmp's LEFT operand, carries 12 real marker lines, and is the only condbr-carrying body for which a CONCRETE ir_eval witness is affordable at all (24.4 s at n = 65, measured; the other has none at any argument).

residue_cost_law_remeasured.claim: ir_wrap w n costs O(n) in the DIVIDEND and is INDEPENDENT of the width w.
residue_cost_law_remeasured.method: One `Eq Nat (ir_wrap w n) n` declaration each in tests/evalir_scratchpad.rs, per-declaration wall clock, same spec build.
residue_cost_law_remeasured.supersedes: The `2^W law` recorded on 2026-08-13 (x15.3 per four bits at W = 8/12/16). Those three timings are real; the law read off them is not, because the dividend there was 2^W - 1 and moved with the width.
residue_cost_law_remeasured.consequence: `wide type => unaffordable` is false; `large CONSTANT => unaffordable` is true. This body is at width 64 with constants 55296/57343/1114112 and chains.
residue_cost_law_remeasured.superseded_by: residue_cost_law_after_the_folding_lemma (2026-08-15). Every row above was measured on an ir_div_go whose guard was ir_nat_ltb, a paired unary walk; the law is TRUE of that definition and the definition changed. Kept, not rewritten: it is the measurement that made this chain exist.

witness_costs_seconds.note: Exactly one concrete ir_eval witness is REGISTERED (n = 65). Any argument whose emitted path reaches bb4 must decide ir_vc_c3, whose dividend is 1114112, i.e. ~7.3 minutes on every Specification::new(). The other three paths are covered by PATH witnesses. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-15: these six rows were measured before the ir_wrap literal-folding lemma and are kept as the record of the wall. Four concrete ir_eval witnesses are now registered (65, 55296, 70000, 1114112) covering every emitted path; see witness_costs_seconds_after_the_folding_lemma.

residue_cost_law_after_the_folding_lemma.claim: ir_wrap w n costs O(w + n/2^w): linear in the QUOTIENT, independent of the DIVIDEND. A residue whose quotient is zero -- every residue any chain in this program forces -- folds in ~0.01 s at any width and any literal.
residue_cost_law_after_the_folding_lemma.lemma: ir_nat_ltb_sub_eq : forall a b, Eq Bool (ir_nat_pos (Nat.sub b a)) (ir_nat_ltb a b). ir_div_go's guard is now ir_nat_ltb_sub; ir_div_go_guard restates the loop's unfolding equation with ir_nat_ltb back in it, so the substitution is kernel-checked rather than read off two definitions. No new accelerated constant: Nat.sub was already the outer operation of ir_nat_rem.
residue_cost_law_after_the_folding_lemma.method: One `Eq Nat (ir_wrap w n) r` declaration each in tests/evalir_scratchpad.rs, per-declaration wall clock. The `before` rows are one process against origin/main@1ec739677; the `after` rows are one process against the same tree plus the lemma.
residue_cost_law_after_the_folding_lemma.consequence: The 24 s that ir_vc_split1 paid on every Specification::new() is 0.010 s, and the ~9.6-day sentinel residue of the fifth chain -- extrapolated, never measured -- is 0.007 s. Three concrete ir_eval witnesses are registered in eval_ir_bvar_range, which had none at any argument.
residue_cost_law_after_the_folding_lemma.what_it_does_NOT_fix: ir_nat_eqb still walks its FIRST operand unary, so the fifth chain's sentinel-TRUE path (end = 4294967295) has no concrete witness. Same technique, different theorem, not proved here.

witness_costs_seconds_after_the_folding_.declined: ir_eval at 55296 (19.106 s), at 70000 (31.404 s) and at 1114112 (210.144 s). All three RUN -- the residue wall is gone -- and all three were declined: covering this body's other condbr edges needs an argument above 0xD800 by construction, so 260 s on every Specification::new() against a lemma that saves 33-107 s of one. The fifth chain's three concrete witnesses ARE registered, at 0.1 s each, because its arguments are small.
witness_costs_seconds_after_the_folding_.why_these_are_not_zero: The residue is no longer the cost: ir_int_cmp compares through ir_nat_ltb, which peels its FIRST operand -- the ARGUMENT -- one Nat.rec layer at a time, so a concrete execution costs about the code point. An ir_nat_ltb lemma of the same shape as ir_nat_ltb_sub_eq is what would make it free; ir_wrap's does not.
witness_costs_seconds_after_the_folding_.method: One declaration each in tests/spec_scratchpad.rs against the full spec, per-declaration wall clock, on a box running six concurrent spec builds -- so these are upper bounds.
witness_costs_seconds_after_the_folding_.note_superseded: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-15 (later, comparison lemmas). The three declined rows below were measured on a box carrying six concurrent spec builds and are upper bounds; the same three declarations are now REGISTERED, and both the walk baseline and the folded run were re-measured on one box in one window -- see witness_costs_seconds_after_the_comparison_lemmas.

full_specification_new_seconds_after_the.headline: A COST, not a saving: +5.13 s of wall and +5.10 s of CPU on a ~215 s Specification::new(), i.e. +2.4%. Three paired rounds, two replicates per side launched TOGETHER so both sides share one window at matched 4-way concurrency; sequential rounds on this box drifted by 20 s and cannot support a 5 s claim.
full_specification_new_seconds_after_the.declaration_count: 6207 -> 6223 (+16): 11 substrate declarations (2 retired, 13 added) and 5 concrete execution witnesses.
full_specification_new_seconds_after_the.where_it_goes: Measured, not attributed. A per-stage clock over all 160 stages on both trees in one window: exactly ONE stage moved -- add_eval_ir_contains, 1.822 -> 7.034 s at the SAME 28 declarations. Inside it: ir_fc_exact 0.893 -> 3.700, ir_fc_never_faults 0.449 -> 2.874, ir_fc_machine_sound 0.460 -> 2.866. That chain's A4 is an Eq.refl at SYMBOLIC bytes and its predicate's head is ir_nat_eqb; a subtraction equality test names BOTH operands TWICE (a-b and b-a) where the walk names each once, so the stuck term compared structurally is about twice the size. add_eval_ir_valid_char went DOWN, 0.651 -> 0.512 s, while gaining three executions.
full_specification_new_seconds_after_the.priced_alternative: Folding ir_nat_ltb alone buys all three is_valid_char witnesses (that body's three comparisons are all ult) at no measurable cost, and leaves the fifth chain's fourth path PATH-only. The trade taken is 5.1 s per full spec build for two executions of an emitted condbr edge no argument could reach before. Both agreement theorems are proved either way: a theorem costs nothing, the DEFINITION the machine runs is what costs.
full_specification_new_seconds_after_the.method: tests/zz_spec_clock-style harness: one Specification::new() per process, wall from Instant::now() around the build and user CPU from /usr/bin/time -p on the whole process.
